experiment.objective: Compare average vehicle wait times between an adaptive neural network traffic signal system and a fixed-timing system at the same intersection
independent_variables: traffic signal system type (adaptive vs fixed)
dependent_variables: number of vehicles passing through intersection
experiment.baseline: Current fixed-timing signal system with 60-second cycles
experiment.procedure: Install two identical traffic signal systems at the same intersection: one with the adaptive neural network controller and one with fixed timing. Collect wait time data simultaneously from both systems during morning rush hour over 30 days. Ensure traffic patterns are consistent between systems by using the same input sensors and timing for data collection.
experiment.expected_result: The adaptive neural network system will show a 15-25% reduction in average vehicle wait time compared to the fixed-timing system after 30 days of operation
experiment.falsification_condition: If the adaptive system shows no statistically significant improvement (p>0.05) in average wait time compared to the fixed-timing system after 30 days of operation, or if performance degrades when encountering new traffic patterns not seen during training
experiment.sample_requirements: Minimum of 1000 vehicle observations per system per day to ensure statistical significance
safety_constraints: Ensure emergency vehicle override functionality remains operational
Maintain minimum green light times for pedestrian safety
Fail-safe mechanisms that revert to fixed timing if neural network malfunctions
experiment.information_gain: This experiment will determine if traffic signals can learn and adapt to traffic patterns through a neural network-like mechanism, potentially revolutionizing traffic management systems if successful
